intended_object: The restriction (comorphism) map on coordinate Hopf algebras, O(Sp₂ₘ) → O(B), where B is the closed subgroup scheme of Sp₂ₘ that stabilizes the standard complete isotropic flag. It is the Hopf algebra surjection dual to the closed immersion B ↪ Sp₂ₘ. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is the canonical quotient morphism `CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient` from the symplectic coordinate Hopf algebra to its quotient by `definingHopfIdeal R m`. The codomain, `coordinateHopfAlgebra R m` on line 111, is defined as exactly that quotient, so the two match by construction.

The ideal is the image of the weight-parabolic ideal with flag-order weights. It is generated by the entries strictly below the diagonal in the order e₀,…,eₘ₋₁,fₘ₋₁,…,f₀ (lemma `definingHopfIdeal_toIdeal`). The file also proves that for any commutative R-algebra A, the A-points of the quotient are exactly the symplectic matrices that are upper triangular in that order (`mem_definingPointsSubgroup_iff` and `pointsMulEquiv`). So the quotient is the coordinate ring of the flag subgroup, and this map is restriction of functions from Sp₂ₘ to that subgroup, i.e. the comorphism of the closed immersion.

The generality is right: R is any commutative ring and m is any natural number, the usual setting for split group schemes. Mathlib has no symplectic group scheme or flag subgroup scheme to compare against.
